title: I built a Multiplayer Space Voxel Sandbox with my 10yo son. 100% of the C# logic, 3D models, textures, and music are AI-generated. Here is our first trailer! (Open Source)
author: KatastrophalKlang
selftext: My 10yo son and I built this open-source voxel game entirely with AI (Claude generated the Code, and models - ChatGPT / Gemini helped with the story - Music by Suno, Soundeffects by Elevenlabs, I managed the Client/Server architecture). **Read the full backstory and find the links to the free Beta & GitHub down in the comments! ⬇️**

replies.author: KatastrophalKlang
replies.body: Thanks a lot! My son is super thrilled to see the first reactions. :)

comments.author: KatastrophalKlang
comments.body:
Hey everyone! 👋

I wanted to share a massive milestone for a project I've been working on with my 10-year-old son. He pitched me his dream game: *Minecraft in space*, with custom spaceships, procedural planets, and base building.

I’m a software architect/CIO with 25 years of experience, but I didn't want to spend my evenings typing boilerplate code. So, we went all-in on GenAI.

**The AI Workflow & Architecture:** I haven't written a single line of code myself. Instead, I used my background purely to enforce a strict **Client/Server architecture** (Unity 6 for rendering/input, .NET 8 Dedicated Server for chunk generation and UDP networking).

* **Code & Logic:** Prompted entirely via Claude and ChatGPT. (AI handles the syntax, I handle the structural boundaries).
* **Music:** Generated with Suno.
* **Soundeffects:** Generated with Elevenlabs.
* **3D Models & Textures:** Completely AI-generated.

Justus (my son) is the Game Designer with the vision, and I steer the AI to build it.

**The Result:** It actually works amazingly well. The game is now in an Early Beta state. We have seamless space flight, arcade minigames, crafting, and multiplayer where players can host their own servers.

We just open-sourced the entire project under the AGPL license!

**Play the Beta & Check the Source:**

* 🪐 **Playable Demo (Windows/Linux):**[https://jumavegames.itch.io/blocks-beyond-the-stars](https://jumavegames.itch.io/blocks-beyond-the-stars)
* 💻 **GitHub (Source Code):**[https://github.com/marceld23/BlocksBeyondTheStars](https://github.com/marceld23/BlocksBeyondTheStars)
* 🌐 **Website:**[https://www.blocksbeyondthestars.com/](https://www.blocksbeyondthestars.com/)

**We are looking for contributors! 🤝** Since we just went open source, our doors are wide open. Whether you are fascinated by AI game dev and want to help with the C#/Unity codebase, create new voxel models, or just playtest the beta and break our server—everyone is welcome! We coordinate completely async via GitHub Discussions.

I’d love to hear your thoughts on the trailer, or if you have any questions about the specific prompting/architecture workflow, ask away! 🚀

replies.author: KatastrophalKlang
replies.body:
Starting with templates and modding is such a great, hands-on way to teach!

It actually touches on a fascinating educational dilemma I think about daily from my professional perspective as a CIO: Back then, modding forced kids to get into the weeds and understand the underlying mechanics. Today, AI abstracts away all that detailed heavy lifting.

For Justus at 10 years old, that’s actually fine - he’s far more interested in the creative side (ideas, game design, visual direction) rather than typing syntax. But from a software engineering standpoint, it creates a real paradox: You **need** deep architectural knowledge to evaluate what the AI just built and spot hidden implications or tech debt. Yet, how do people gain that deep foundational knowledge if the AI does all the detailed coding for them?

Since you have a background in teaching game dev, how do you think we can teach future junior developers that critical, deep understanding when tools (seemingly!) generate flawless code out of the box? I'd love to hear your take on this!
